Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
It really depends on what you're interested in.
We have plenty of museum of course, ranging from medieval to modern art, nice architecture etc. It also depends on your budget: for example there's a  very nice restaurant on the Eiffel Tower, but it costs at least 180€ per person...

Anyway, visiting places like l' Île de la Cité and Notre-Dame, going to the Eiffel Tower, cruising on the Seine with the " fly-boats ", going in good restaurants are must-do.
You can do some shopping too at  Les Galleries Lafayette or  Le Printemps (where there is a very nice tea-room under an  Art Nouveau dome or at the avenue Montaigne (near the Champs Elysées).

The quartier Latin (near La sorbonne, Saint-Michel and Notre-Dame) is very nice too though a bit touristic like Montmartre (and the Sacré-Coeur which is not worth imho the visit).

Avoid the 20th and 16th arrondissement that are mostly residential.

Prince of Paris, France

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body:
The Mont Saint Michel is definitely worth seeing, but it is 350km west from Paris. There must 1-day tours there from Paris. Otherwise, if you rent a car, you can spend a night there: first visit the Mont itself, then drive along the bay up to Cancale, a nice oyster farming village, and Saint Malo, a XVIIth century military and privateer port. Spend the night in Cancale of Saint Malo (not in the Mont, it's horrendously expensive), finish visiting the next morning then come back.

If you go to Germany, you should try to have a step in Strasbourg as well. Very nice city center and pink stone cathedral. The food is very nice there too.

+1 for Bruges and Ghent in Belgium.

And I don't know if you wrote that off your trip on purpose, but London is only 2 hours away from Paris or Bruxels by train. If you come to London, we play on monday nights.

That's true, but both Paris and London have enough must-see to fill two week of vacations alone. People trying to do multiples country in one vacation never cease to amaze me, even if I understand most peoples can't pay an oversea vacation every two year.

As far as wine go, the "easy" way to get local and good wine is to tour small winery ; often they offer to taste for free, and often it's near impossible to spot the difference with better-known wine while they cost between five and ten time less. Problem is, thoses winery aren't in Paris, often don't advertise much, and may not alway speak english. In Paris itself, it may be possible, but it's a lot harder to find in my experience, because you often have mainly very well-known wine, which are often very good but very expansive.

Messages.Author: brandonsantacruz
Messages.Body:
Hi Bestie,
I went back to Europe last year and went to Turkey, CZ, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, and Croatia. All great places for their own reasons. Here's a quick intro: Use Rick Steve's guides including Central Europe and some that are country specific. He has good videos on Youtube, too: www.youtube.com/user/RickSteves

All of these cities are good for walking, so bring good shoes! Pack light, like Rick says. Avoid suitcases if at all possible, just bring a backpack. Use a money belt for added confidence around areas that you might otherwise get pickpocketed. Do not buy package deals from the visitor centers anywhere, they are a ripoff.You will never be able to do all that stuff to make it worthwhile.

CZ- I was in Prague and Chezky Krumlov (sorry for bad spelling). Saw Mucha's artwork, which was a highlight. Chesky has a good museum, too. Lots of old buildings, info about soviet occupation.

I'll come back to this later, need to serve dinner.

Messages.Author: brandonsantacruz
Messages.Body:
All of these cities have interesting events going on. I actually found an English language comedy show in Prague through Facebook. Do some research and you never know what random stuff will pop up. Czech goulash with dumplings is the best, take my word for it. The Jewish Quarter is very interesting because they were able to save much of the historical stuff during the Holocaust. Very somber and informative.

Vienna, Austria of course has good museums. The Prater was a fun nighttime diversion. The metro is excellent. Trip adviser led me to a gamer bar on the other side of town that had free nachos that night. I saw Jezebelle at the opera house in the standing room section for a bargain of a few Euros. Get there very early and stake out a spot on the railing with your scarf. Don't stand behind a tall person.

Spent just two nights in Bratislava, Slovakia and happened to be there during a craft brew festival. Craft beer making is very new there and there were some snobby Austrians who punctuated the fact that they mostly like weak, plain beer there. It was cool to see Devin Castle by bus, which was originally built during the Iron Age. Napoleon blew it up because he was pissed at the Slovaks. He also left some cannonballs in the old down Bratislava walls.

Hungary is very different from everywhere else I went in Central Europe. The Magyar influence combined with the neo-fascist government keeps things interesting. The past is hotly contested here given the collusion with both the Nazis and the Soviets. New monuments are build while large sections of buildings slough away. Incongruous to say the least. The best meal I had in Europe this time I found after doing an Airbnb "experience" wine tasting with "Mikki." I had the Hungarian boar and pork will never be the same. The House of Terror was great, but try to find a time when it is not busy or you will be stuck in line in the basement forever. Played VTES here, which was fun. Could have probably timed things better and included VTES in Austria, CZ, and Croatia, too. The Grand Bazaar is good to walk through, especially for touristy stuff on the top floor or for supplies for a picnic on the bottom.

In Croatia Zagreb was cool to walk around, as was Zadar. I wasn't in Split for long enough to appreciate it and Dubrovnic is a combination of way too many tourists and locals who are tired of them. Plitzvice (sp) national park is great. Prepare for an unbelievable crowded, touristy, slow walk through a beautiful park. The sea is super salty to the point where you may not enjoy it, even if it looks great.

What to drink in these countries:
Istanbul- Raki
Cz- Beer!
Austria/Slovakia- Wine>beer
Hungary- Palinka or wine
Croatia- Wine >> Beer

That's my quick review, I hope it is helpful. Rick Steves for details. I did Airbnb all the way, except for Istanbul.Worked out.
